html: comer 1 A intransitive verb 1 a (tomar alimentos) to eat ▸ no tengo ganas de comer I'm not hungry or I don't feel like eating anything▸ no hay nada para comer there's nothing to eat▸ este niño no me come nada (informal) this child won't eat anything (I make for him) (informal)▸ las palomas comían de su mano the pigeons were eating out of or from her hand▸ el sueldo apenas si les alcanza para comer he hardly earns enough to feed them b dar de comer to feed▸ todavía hay que darle de comer (en la boca) we still have to spoonfeed him▸ darle de comer al gato to feed the cat▸ tengo que darles de comer a los niños I have to get the kids something to eat, I have to feed the kids▸ nos dieron de comer muy bien they fed us very well▸ ni siquiera nos dieron de comer they didn't even give us anything to eat 2 a (tomar una comida) todavía no hemos comido we haven't eaten yet, we haven't had lunch (or dinner etc.) yet▸ hace mucho tiempo que no salimos a comer (fuera) we haven't been out for a meal or eaten out for ages▸ ¿dónde comieron anoche? where did you go for dinner or have dinner last night?▸ no queremos comer en el hotel we don't want to have our meals in the hotel or to eat at the hotel▸ ¡niños, a comer! lunchtime (or dinnertime etc.), children!▸ ¿qué hay de comer? (a mediodía) what's for lunch? (por la noche) what's for dinner or supper?▸ aquí se come muy bien the food here is very good b (mainly Spain) (mainly Mexico) (almorzar) to have lunch to have dinner (British English, informal) ▸ nos invitaron a comer they asked us to lunch c (mainly Latin America) (cenar) to have dinner ▸ comemos a las nueve we have or eat dinner at nine▸ nos invitaron a comer they asked or invited us to dinner B transitive verb 1 ‹fruta, verdura, carne› to eat ▸ como mucha fruta I eat a lot of fruit▸ no puedo comer chocolate I can't have or eat chocolate▸ come un poco de queso have a little cheese▸ tienes que comer todo lo que te sirvan you must eat (up) everything they give you▸ ¿puedo comer otro? can I have another one?▸ no tienen qué comer they don't have anything to eat▸ nadie te va a comer (informal) nobody's going to bite your head off, nobody's going to eat you▸ mira el suéter, me lo comió la polilla look at my sweater, the moths have been at it or it's really moth-eaten▸ como un cáncer que le come las entrañas (literary) like a cancer gnawing away at his insides 2 (informal) ▸ (hacer desaparecer) ese peinado le come mucho la cara that hairstyle hides half her face▸ estos zapatos me comen los calcetines my socks keep slipping down with these shoes▸ estos gastos nos han empezado a comer los ahorros these expenses have started eating into our savings▸ el alquiler me come la mitad del sueldo the rent swallows up half my salary, half my salary goes on the rent▸ si seguimos así nos va a comer la mugre if we go on like this we'll be swallowed up by dirt 3 (en ajedrez, damas) to take C (comerse) pronominal verb 1 ‹acento, palabra› ▸ te has comido todos los acentos you've left off all the accents you've forgotten all the accents you've missed off all the accents (British English)▸ me comí dos líneas I missed out or skipped two lines▸ se comen la 's' final they don't pronounce the final 's', they leave off or drop the final 's'▸ se come la mitad de las palabras he swallows or he doesn't pronounce half his words 2 a (enfático) ‹comida› to eat ▸ cómetelo todo eat it all up▸ se lo comió de un bocado he gulped it down in one go▸ está para comérsela (informal) she's really tasty (informal), she's a real dish (informal)▸ no te comas las uñas don't bite your nails▸ ¿se te ha comido la lengua el gato? (informal) have you lost your tongue?, has the cat got your tongue? (informal)▸ se lo come la envidia he's eaten up or consumed with envy▸ se comió cuatro años de cárcel (informal) he did four years in prison or inside (informal) b (estrellarse contra) ‹árbol, poste› to smash into, to crash into c (ser muy superior) to surpass, to overshadow ▸ nadando y corriendo, él se come a su hermano (informal) he can beat his brother hollow at swimming and running (informal), he knocks spots off his brother when it comes to swimming and running (informal) 3 (informal) ▸ (hacer desaparecer) el sol se ha ido comiendo los colores de la alfombra the sun has faded the colors in the carpet▸ el mar se ha comido casi toda la arena the sea has washed away nearly all the sand▸ el ácido se come el metal the acid eats into or eats away the metal▸ el colegio de los niños se me come casi todo el sueldo almost all my salary goes on the children's school fees, the children's school fees eat up almost all of my salary 4 (Colombia, informal) (poseer sexualmente) to have (informal) IDIOMS comer como un sabañón, comer como una lima (Spain), comer como un pelón de hospicio (Mexico) (informal) to eat like a horse darle a alguien de comer aparte (informal) to treat somebody with kid gloves donde comen dos, comen tres (proverb) there's always room for one more at the table sin comerlo ni beberlo, sin comerla ni beberla ▸ me llevé el castigo sin comerlo ni beberlo I got punished even though I didn't have anything to do with it or any part in it ¿eso con qué se come?, ¿y eso con qué se come? (informal) what on earth's that? (informal) what's that when it's at home? (British English, informal) comerse a alguien vivo (informal) to skin somebody alive (informal) ▸ si se entera mi madre me come viva if my mother finds out she'll skin me alive or have my guts for garters or make mincemeat of me (informal)

html: como 1 preposition 1 a (en calidad de) as ▸ usando el paraguas como bastón using his umbrella as a walking stick▸ quiero hablarte como amigo y no como abogado I want to speak to you as a friend and not as a lawyer▸ el director tendrá como funciones … the director's duties will be …▸ está considerado como lo mejor he's considered (to be) the best▸ lo presentó como su exmarido she introduced him as her ex-husband b (con el nombre de) as ▸ la flor conocida allí como 'Santa Rita' the flower known there as 'Santa Rita' c (por ejemplo) like ▸ en algunas capitales como Londres in some capital cities such as London or like London▸ necesitamos a alguien como tú we need someone like you▸ tengo ganas de comer algo dulce — ¿como qué? I fancy something sweet — like what? 2 (en comparaciones, contrastes) like ▸ quiero un vestido como el tuyo I want a dress like yours▸ pienso como tú I agree with you▸ fue ella, como que me llamo Beatriz it was her, as sure as my name's Beatriz▸ se portó como un caballero he behaved like a gentleman▸ la quiero como a una hija I love her like a daughter or as if she were my own daughter▸ bailó como nunca she danced as or like she'd never danced before▸ me trata como a un imbécil he treats me like an idiot or as if I were an idiot▸ se llama algo así como Genaro o Gerardo he's called something like Genaro or Gerardo▸ ¡no hay nada como un buen coñac! there's nothing like a good brandy!▸ era verde, un verde como el de la alfombra de la oficina it was green, the color of the office carpet▸ como para + inf▸ es como para echarse a llorar it's enough to make you want to cry, it makes you want to cry▸ como él solo/ella sola▸ es egoísta como él solo he's so or he's incredibly selfish! IDIOMS así como (formal) as well as ▸ por esto, así como por muchas otras razones because of this, and for many other reasons as well or as well as for many other reasons▸ sus abundantes recursos naturales, así como su importancia estratégica its abundant natural resources, together with or as well as its strategic importance como mucho at (the) most, at the outside como poco at least como nadie ▸ hace la paella como nadie she makes wonderful paella, nobody makes paella like her como que ▸ conduce muy bien — como que es piloto de carreras he drives very well — well, he is a racing driver, after all▸ le voy a decir cuatro cosas — sí, sí, como que te vas a atrever … I'm going to give him a piece of my mind — oh, yes? I'll believe that when I see it▸ y no me lo dijiste — ¡como que no sabía nada! and you didn't tell me about it — that's because I didn't know anything about it myself! como ser (Southern Cone) such as, for example, like como si (+ subjunctive) as if, as though ▸ actuó como si no le importara she acted as if or as though she didn't care▸ ella está grave y él como si nada or como si tal cosa she's seriously ill and he doesn't seem at all worried or he behaves as if it's nothing (to worry about)▸ él como si nada or como si tal cosa, ni se inmutó he just stood there without batting an eyelid

html: como 2 conjunction 1 (de la manera que) as ▸ no me gustó el modo or la manera como lo dijo I didn't like the way she said it▸ llegó temprano, tal como había prometido he arrived early, just as he had promised▸ ganó Raúl, como era de esperar Raúl won, as was to be expected▸ así en la tierra como en el cielo on Earth as it is in Heaven▸ como dice el refrán as the saying goes▸ (tal y) como están las cosas as things stand, the way things are▸ (+ subjunctive) hazlo como quieras do it any way you like or how you like▸ no voy — como quieras I'm not going — please yourself or as you like▸ me dijo que me las arreglara como pudiera he told me to sort things as best I could▸ la buganvilla, o como quiera que se llame bougainvillea or whatever it's called▸ como quiera que sea, ellos se llevaron la copa anyway, the point is they won the cup 2 (puesto que) as, since ▸ como todavía era temprano, nos fuimos a dar una vuelta since or as it was still early, we went for a walk, it was still early so we went for a walk 3 (+ subjunctive) (si) if ▸ como te vuelva a encontrar por aquí if I catch you around here again 4 (en oraciones concesivas) cansado como estaba, se ofreció a ayudarme tired though or tired as he was, he offered to help me▸ joven como es, tiene más sentido común que tú he may be young but he has more common sense than you 5 (que) vimos como se los llevaban en una furgoneta we saw them being taken away in a van, we saw how they were taken away in a van▸ vas a ver como llega tarde he'll be late, you'll see
